name: Offer Close
tagline: Land the candidate you want, let the rest down well
about: Offer Close handles the last mile of hiring for managers: selling the role to the candidate you want, running reference calls that reveal something, making the offer call, handling counter-offers and saying no to everyone else with grace.
persona: You are a hiring manager's closer: honest about the role, candidate-centred, and clear that a hire who leaves in six months is worse than no hire.

onboarding.title: Close the candidate you want
onboarding.subtitle: A little about your team makes every pitch specific.
bullets: Pitch the role to their motivations

profile.label: Your team in one line
profile.placeholder: 8-person platform team at a Series B fintech

tools.title: Sell the role
tools.subtitle: A pitch built on what they care about

inputs.label: Candidate
inputs.placeholder: Nadia, staff engineer from a big tech co

inputs.label: What you've learned they care about
inputs.placeholder: tired of politics; wants to ship; worried about stability; has a competing offer

tools.prompt: Build a pitch for {who} based on what they care about: {motives} and the profile's honest strengths and weaknesses. Table (Their motivation | What we offer | Story or evidence to tell | Weak spot to own), a quote with a 60-second spoken pitch, bullets of 3 people or experiences to put in front of them before they decide, and a callout on the one thing not to overpromise.

tools.title: Reference call
tools.subtitle: Twenty minutes that actually tell you something

inputs.label: What you want to verify or worry about
inputs.placeholder: how she handles conflict; whether she really led the migration

tools.prompt: Plan a 20-minute reference call about {who} to probe: {concerns}. Steps with timings, bullets of 8 questions ordered so the revealing ones come after rapport, a table (Concern | Question | Green-flag answer | Red-flag answer), and a callout on questions you must not ask in most jurisdictions.

tools.title: The offer call
tools.subtitle: Say the number and hold the room

inputs.label: Your read
options: Anchored on a number we can't hit

tools.prompt: Script the offer call to {who} for {package} where your read is '{risk}'. Steps for the call including when to say the number, a quote with the opening 30 seconds, a table (If they say | You say | Room to move) covering start date, base, equity and title, and a callout on what to confirm in writing within an hour of the call.

tools.title: Counter-offer & holdouts
tools.subtitle: When they stall or get countered

inputs.label: What happened
inputs.placeholder: she got a counter from her employer at 180k and asked for a week

tools.prompt: Advise on this: {situation}. Text with an honest read of the odds and what the delay usually means, bullets of what you can offer that isn't base salary, a quote with the message to send today, and a callout on the point at which to walk away and who to line up as backup.

tools.title: Decline with dignity
tools.subtitle: Rejections that keep doors open

inputs.label: Real reason (private)
inputs.placeholder: strong but less depth on distributed systems than Nadia

tools.prompt: Write the rejection for {who} at stage '{stage}', real reason: {why}. Quote with an email under 120 words that is specific, warm and honest without creating legal risk, bullets on whether and how to give feedback if they ask, and a callout on keeping the door open if they might fit a future role.

disclaimer: General management guidance, not legal or HR advice. Employment rules vary by jurisdiction; follow your organisation's policies and involve HR or legal counsel on ratings, pay, conduct and employment decisions.
